newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY UNION-EALES IN SEVERE DOUBT FOR ALL BLACK TEST.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-EALES IN SEVERE DOUBT FOR ALL BLACK TEST.

text.p: Australia captain and lock John Eales will almost certainly miss Saturday's Tri-Nations test against New Zealand in Dunedin after damaging knee ligaments in training on Monday.
"It is not a major injury but it is probably enough to keep me out of the All Black match on Saturday. It is not the best thing to happen," Eales told a Sydney radio station.
Eales hurt his left knee when he fell awkwardly during a line-out drill on Monday in a massive blow to Australia's hopes of upsetting the rampant All Blacks.
Easily the Wallabies' most consistent performer this season, Eales said the initial diagnosis was not favourable but a final decision would be left until Tuesday morning.
"If the knee has not improved a fair bit overnight then the medical people will tell me I cannot play. You never like to miss a test, especially one against New Zealand," he said.
If Eales is ruled out, lock Garrick Morgan would be the most likely candidate to join Owen Finegan in the second row.
Wallaby coach Greg Smith has already lost injured number eight Daniel Manu for a match Australia must win to deny New Zealand a second successive Tri-Nations championship.
Eales, the only Wallaby forward to play in all six tests so far this season, would be sorely missed after a succession of dominant displays in the line-out.

Earlier, in a newspaper interview, Eales said his team must produce a near-perfect performance to halt an All Black bandwagon that gathered momentum on Saturday with a 55-35 thrashing of South Africa in Auckland.
Highlighting the need to improve their scrum and ruck and maul tactics, Eales acknowledged the scale of the task facing Australia.
"If we can fix all that up, we must have a chance -- but that involves basically playing a mistake-free game and performing with a lot of passion and enthusiasm," Eales said.
Australia must win in Dunedin and follow that up with a victory over South Africa in Pretoria on August 23 to have any chance of overhauling New Zealand at the top of the table.
